a2-unit-44.44.1 The Life Hacks podcast:
Host: Hi everyone! Welcome to Life Hacks, the show that makes your life easier. I'm here with Rafael, and today we're talking about clothes and shoes.
Rafael: That's right. Our listeners sent us lots of questions. The first one is from Kate. She says, I'm always losing socks in the washing machine. What can I do?
Host: This one's easy! Keep your socks together in the washing machine by putting them in a mesh bag. That's what I do at home.
Rafael: And speaking of losing things, Tom asks, how can I stop my buttons from falling off? Tom, to stop buttons from falling off your clothes, you can paint the threads with clear nail polish.
Host: Good tip! Next, Lucy asks, what do you suggest for a stuck zipper on my backpack? Lucy, in order to get a stuck zipper moving again, rub it with a candle or a pencil. I tried it last week, and it worked!
Rafael: Our next question is from Priya. She hates ironing. For fewer wrinkles, some people put a few ice cubes in the dryer for a few minutes. People say this works because the ice melts and turns into steam, and the steam helps with the wrinkles.
Host: Interesting! Now, shoes. Ana in São Paulo says, my shoes smell bad, but I don't want to wash them. Ana, in order to remove bad smells from your shoes, put dry tea bags inside them and leave them overnight.
Rafael: And Paulo in New York asks, how can I keep my feet dry when it rains? Paulo, rub your canvas sneakers with melted beeswax to make them more waterproof. You can buy it at craft stores or online.
Host: Lots of people asked about dirty white sneakers. For super white sneakers, put a little toothpaste on an old toothbrush and clean them with it.
Rafael: One more question. Carol says, my new shoes are a little tight. You can make tight shoes more comfortable by putting wet newspaper inside them and leaving them to dry.
Host: That's a new one for me! Thanks for all your questions. Next week, we're talking about home hacks. Bye!
